claims.text: An MLP trained on ab initio molecular-dynamics data can improve the representation of multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states near melting.
The proposed MLP training produces improved atomic-configuration representation.
The MLP can capture complex many-body interactions.
Capturing complex many-body interactions enhances phase-space overlap between the reference and ab initio target systems.
Enhanced reference–target phase-space overlap reduces thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The MLP will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The free-energy difference between the solid and liquid phases can serve as the measure of thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The proposed method is applicable to both equiatomic and non-equiatomic multicomponent alloys.
The applicable alloys contain three to six principal elements.
The applicable temperature range is 0.8–1.2 times the melting temperature.
The effectiveness of the MLP may depend on the quality and quantity of its training data.
The effectiveness of the MLP may depend on alloy composition and temperature.
The benchmark compares thermodynamic-integration calculations using MLP and EAM reference systems.
The hypothesis is falsified if the MLP fails to reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by at least 20% relative to the EAM reference.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome requires at least a 30% mismatch reduction, whereas the falsification rule rejects the hypothesis only below 20%. A result from 20% to less than 30% would fail the stated prediction but would not falsify the hypothesis, so the benchmark is not decisive for the quantitative claim.
